text: dsh-model-key-sync 是面向 DSH 网页端的模型配置与密钥同步插件。它通过设置页和 agent 工具导出、恢复自定义模型提供方，并可把配置同步到 S3 兼容存储或 WebDAV。用户可以查看本机模型摘要、手动测试远端、上传或拉取配置，也可以开启模型变更后的自动上传；拉取会合并提供方，并提供冲突时的强制选项。API 密钥同步可单独关闭，默认开启；启用后密钥会以明文形式存放在所配置的远端。

dsh-model-key-sync syncs custom DSH model providers through its web settings page and agent tool. It exports, restores, tests, pushes and pulls configuration using S3 or WebDAV. Pull merges routes. API-key sync defaults on, can be disabled, and stores synced keys as plaintext remotely.
想把 DSH 里配置的自定义模型提供方同步到另一台电脑。
有没有办法把模型配置和对应的 API 密钥备份到自己的 WebDAV 或 S3 存储？
I want to move my custom DSH model routes between computers using cloud storage.
dsh-model-key-sync 的功能「模型配置云端同步」：在设置页选择 S3 兼容存储或 WebDAV 后，可测试连接、上传本机模型提供方配置或从远端拉取并合并；密钥同步可单独开关。
dsh-model-key-sync: test S3 or WebDAV, push model routes, or pull and merge them. API-key sync has a toggle.
dsh-model-key-sync 使用前须知：API 密钥同步默认开启；启用时密钥会上传并以明文保存在配置的 S3 或 WebDAV 远端，可关闭密钥同步只传模型声明。

dsh-model-key-sync README · dsh-model-key-sync：Sync your **DeepSeek Harness model configuration and third-party API keys** across machines, over S3-compatible storage or WebDAV. Sign in to Harness on a new computer, pull once, and your custom providers and their keys are there — no retyping one key per provider.

dsh-model-key-sync README · dsh-model-key-sync：> ### Keys are stored in the remote as plaintext
>
> This is deliberate — it matches CC Switch, and it means a new machine needs no
> passphrase. The consequence is blunt: **anyone who can read that bucket or
> collection can read every API key in it.** Use a dedicated application password,
> keep the cloud account itself safe, and turn the key toggle off if you only want
> model declarations to travel. See [Security](#security).

dsh-model-key-sync README · Why this exists：Harness keeps each machine's profile, credentials and model declarations locally.
Moving to a second machine normally means re-entering every provider: display name,
endpoint, protocol, model catalog, and the key.

dsh-model-key-sync README · Why this exists：Other plugins in the ecosystem sync the profile directory and local plugin sources —
[`dsh-cloud-sync`](https://github.com/dickpy/dsh-cloud-sync) documents that it
deliberately does **not** copy plaintext credentials. That leaves exactly this gap:
the keys. This plugin fills it, and carries the model declarations that reference
them.

dsh-model-key-sync README · Install：Ask the agent in Harness:

> Install the plugin from github:tesths/dsh-model-key-sync

It runs the bundle installer for you. Or point it at a local checkout:

> Install the plugin at /path/to/dsh-model-key-sync

Then reload the page. The section appears under **Settings → Model Key Sync**.

Requires a Harness build that provides the `settings`, `credentials` and `tools`
services, and an `llm-pi-ai` (or compatible) model adapter row.
dsh-model-key-sync README · Configure：**Settings → Model Key Sync**. Cloud sync is the page; a read-only summary of this machine — display name, API endpoint and model count — sits below it.

dsh-model-key-sync README · WebDAV：| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Backend | WebDAV |
| Collection URL | `https://dav.jianguoyun.com/dav/` (nutstore), or your Nextcloud path |
| User name | the account's login name (for nutstore: your email) |
| Password | an **application password**, not the login password |
| Remote directory | `dsh-model-key-sync` |
| Sync group | any name; **identical on every machine** |

dsh-model-key-sync README · S3-compatible：R2, OSS, B2, MinIO and AWS all work. Fill bucket, region (`auto` for R2), endpoint
(blank for AWS), access key id and secret.

Fill in the fields and press **Save** (configuration and secret save together), then **Test** → **Upload**.

dsh-model-key-sync README · On the second machine：Install the plugin, open the same page, fill the **same** values including the sync
group, and press **Pull**. The status card lists the credentials it
stored, for example:

```
pulled
credentials: ACME_API_KEY, OTHER_API_KEY
```

dsh-model-key-sync README · Daily use：- **Manual**: upload after editing models under Settings → Models; pull before using another machine.
- **Auto**: tick *Auto upload*. A pull never triggers an
  upload.
- **Conflict**: nothing is overwritten silently. When both sides changed, a pull is
  refused and the message names the axis — `model routes`, `API keys`, or both. Tick
  *Force* to take the remote, or upload to keep this device.

dsh-model-key-sync README · What travels：| Included | Not included |
| --- | --- |
| Provider routes: display name, protocol, endpoint, model catalog, key reference, provider defaults (reasoning, input, cache, thinking budgets) | Sessions, attachments, plugin sources |
| The API key each route's `apiKeyEnv` resolves to | Credits/quota, usage history |
| Your choice of cloud backend and sync group | Other settings (theme, shortcuts, …) |

dsh-model-key-sync README · What travels：Restoring merges by route name and **preserves fields it did not export** — retry
policy, timeouts, transport or compatibility switches stay as they are on this
machine.

dsh-model-key-sync README · Remote layout：```
<remoteRoot>/v1/<syncGroup>/
├── manifest.json        format, version, device, per-object sha256 and size, snapshotId
├── <provider>.json      one file per route
└── keys.json            { "ENV_NAME": "value" }

dsh-model-key-sync README · Remote layout：Payload objects are written first and the manifest last, so a reader never sees a
manifest describing objects the writer has not finished uploading. Every object is
verified by size and SHA-256 on download. Transfers are serialized with a total
timeout, an idle timeout and a response-size cap.

dsh-model-key-sync README · Security：- Keys leave the machine only through `ctx.credentials.resolve` and are stored
  through `ctx.credentials.set` — the same seam the model adapter reads.
- They are uploaded **unencrypted**. Treat the remote as a secret store: a private
  bucket, an application password you can revoke, no shared folders.
- Turn off *Sync keys* to sync model declarations only.
- Anyone who obtains the remote can use your keys. Revoke them at the provider if
  that happens.
- The local sync state (`~/.dsh/model-key-sync/cloud-state.json`) stores hashes, not
  keys.

dsh-model-key-sync README · Development：```bash
npm install
npm test                 # node test/host.mjs && node test/client.mjs
node test/host.mjs       # 116 checks: settings, files, command channel, keys, S3 + WebDAV
node test/client.mjs     # 91 checks: one-page cloud sync, read-only local summary, command channel

dsh-model-key-sync README · Development：`test/host.mjs` starts a real S3-compatible server and a real WebDAV server on
loopback and drives two simulated devices through upload, pull, idempotency, conflict
refusal and forced overwrite. `test/client.mjs` loads the real client bundle into
jsdom with a faithful `configForms`/`locale`/`slots` contract.

See [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) for why the page talks to the Host
the way it does, and [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before changing that channel.
